question: A 55-year-old man presents to his primary care physician for a wellness checkup. The patient has a past medical history of alcohol abuse and is currently attending alcoholics anonymous with little success. He is currently drinking roughly 1L of hard alcohol every day and does not take his disulfiram anymore. Which of the following findings is most likely to also be found in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Chronic alcohol abuse -> decreased CNS NMDA activity -> 80% CHAIN: Chronic alcohol abuse -> vitamin B1 deficiency -> decreased CNS NMDA activity -> 70% CHAIN: Chronic alcohol abuse -> vitamin B1 deficiency -> Wernicke's encephalopathy -> decreased CNS NMDA activity -> 60% CHAIN: Chronic alcohol abuse -> liver cirrhosis -> decreased transketolase activity -> 50% CHAIN: Chronic alcohol abuse -> liver cirrhosis -> decreased transketolase activity -> microcytic anemia -> 80%
analysis: Given the patient's history of alcohol abuse and current high alcohol consumption, the most likely finding in this patient would be microcytic anemia.
